claims.text: YBCO can exhibit superconducting properties at low temperatures.
YBCO's superconducting properties are due to its crystalline structure and copper-oxide planes.
Copper-oxide planes facilitate the flow of superconducting current through YBCO.
The initial polycrystalline YBCO has a critical temperature of 93 K.
The initial polycrystalline YBCO contains copper-oxide planes in its crystal structure.
Cooling YBCO below its critical temperature in a magnetic field induces the tested superconducting state.
The relevant operating range is 4.2 K to 93 K and 0 T to 10 T.
Copper-oxide planes in YBCO facilitate the formation of Cooper pairs.
Cooper-pair formation in YBCO involves exchange of phonons having an energy of approximately 10 meV.
The proposed phonon exchange produces an attractive electron-electron interaction of approximately 1 meV.
Polycrystalline YBCO will have a critical current density of 1050 A/cm^2 at 4.2 K and 0 T.
The predicted critical current density is approximately 57% higher than the stated baseline.
The baseline critical current density of polycrystalline YBCO is 667 A/cm^2 at 4.2 K and 0 T.
The hypothesis applies to polycrystalline YBCO having a critical temperature between 90 K and 95 K and containing copper-oxide planes.
Differences in synthesis protocols or crystal structure may cause variations in material properties and the predicted critical current density.
